name: Organic search for a store (SEO audit, keyword map, collection and product pages, quick wins and long builds)
asked_as: do an SEO audit of my store
why don't we rank on Google
how do I get more organic traffic
which keywords should we go after
outcome: The owner knows which pages can win which searches and why, has the quick wins ready to paste into the store this week, and has a 90-day build for one product cluster with dates to read the results in Search Console. Every change is ranked by the gross profit of the pages it touches.
first_principles: Store organic revenue comes from pages that match buying searches: collections and sub-collections first, product pages second. A blog pays only in four shapes (this vs that, alternatives to, best X for Y, buying guides) and only when it links early to the page that sells.

Value a search term by profit, not volume: monthly searches x click share at the position you can really reach x conversion rate x gross profit per order. A cost per click above zero is proof the term earns money for someone.

Order of operations is fixed: indexed, then ranked, then clicked. Copy cannot help a page Google has not indexed or has folded into a duplicate. On Shopify the usual leaks are collection-path product URLs, indexed tag and variant pages, and supplier-copied descriptions.

The fastest money sits on pages already at positions 4 to 15 with real impressions: a sharper title, a short intro, and internal links from strong pages move them in weeks. New pages take months. Links take longest and are the only lever that closes a true authority gap.

The live results page decides the page type. If the top results are category grids, a blog post will not rank there; if they are guides, a collection will not. Read the results before choosing what to build.

Search Console is the ground truth; third-party volumes are estimates. Split branded from non-branded clicks before judging anything, because brand growth from ads and word of mouth often hides flat SEO. A page that holds its position but loses clicks has a click problem (AI answers, shopping units), not a ranking problem.

questions.ask: What should search do for you first?
questions.why: A recovery is a technical and change-history job; growth is a keyword and page job; a new category is a long build.

options.label: More sales from searches you nearly win
options.con: capped by demand the store already touches

options.label: Win a category you don't rank for yet
options.con: 3 to 6 months before it shows

options.label: Recover traffic that fell
options.con: needs the cause found before any new work

questions.default: More sales from searches you nearly win, plus one cluster to build
skip_if: brief names a category to win
questions.settle_with_data: Compare non-branded clicks for the last 3 months with the same 3 months a year ago in Search Console. A fall of about a fifth or more, or a drop on a date that matches a site change or a Google update, makes it a recovery job; otherwise read the near-win pages.

questions.ask: Which products should search sell first?
questions.why: SEO effort works when it goes to one product cluster for a quarter; spread thin it moves nothing.

options.label: The cluster with the most gross profit and search demand
options.pro: most money per hour of work
options.con: may not be the owner's favourite line

options.label: Your bestsellers by revenue
options.con: may already rank or have thin margin

options.label: A new or growing line
options.con: less proof it converts from search

questions.default: The cluster with the most gross profit x non-branded impressions
skip_if: the store has one product line
questions.settle_with_data: Join the SKU profit sheet (or order export with costs) to Search Console impressions by collection and product URL; pick the collection with the highest gross profit per month x impressions at positions 4 to 30.

questions.ask: Who will make the changes in the store?
questions.why: Theme fixes (canonicals, grid links, breadcrumbs, schema) need code; titles, intros and collections do not. It decides whether the plan includes a developer list.

options.label: You or your team, from paste-ready sheets
options.con: theme code fixes wait

options.label: A developer for theme fixes, you for copy
options.con: developer time and a test theme

options.label: Copy and settings only, no theme edits
options.pro: no risk to the live theme
options.con: some leaks stay open

questions.default: Paste-ready sheets for the owner plus a short developer list, each fix tested on a copy of the theme

questions.ask: Which countries should search win buyers in?
questions.why: More than one country or language means hreflang, local terms and separate keyword maps.

options.label: Your main selling country
options.con: ignores other demand

options.label: Every country you ship to
options.con: more pages, slower

questions.default: The country with the most orders
questions.settle_with_data: Search Console Performance by country and Shopify orders by ship-to country; add a second market only if it holds a real share of non-branded impressions and orders.

data_map.question: Which pages nearly win?
data_map.data: Pages and queries at positions 4 to 15 with the most impressions, last 3 months
data_map.tool: node tools/ask-knowledge.mjs "search console quick wins positions 4 to 15" --module SEO
data_map.if_missing: no quick-win list; plan rests on new pages

data_map.question: Do our snippets earn their clicks?
data_map.data: The store's own click rate by position bucket (1, 2-3, 4-6, 7-10, 11-20), then each page and query against it
data_map.if_missing: use the title and intent check by hand on the top 20 pages

data_map.question: How big is demand by category?
data_map.data: Monthly searches and cost per click for each collection's main term and its variants; seasonality
data_map.where: Keyword Planner, Google Trends, Search Console impressions
data_map.if_missing: rank by Search Console impressions only

data_map.question: Which page type wins each term, and who ranks?
data_map.data: Top 10 results per money term: page type (grid, product, guide, list), domain, word count above and below the grid, products shown
data_map.where: live results page in the target country
data_map.if_missing: never skip; it decides the page type

data_map.question: Is everything that sells indexed?
data_map.data: Page indexing reasons, sitemap URL count vs crawl count, canonicals on product and collection templates, collection-path product links

data_map.if_missing: URL Inspection on the top 20 pages by revenue

data_map.data: Organic landing pages x purchases x gross profit, 12 months
data_map.where: GA4 joined to the SKU profit sheet
data_map.if_missing: Shopify sales by landing page with an assumed margin, labelled as such

look_for: Branded vs non-branded first: if non-branded clicks are flat and brand clicks grew, the store has a brand win and an SEO problem.
A few landing pages bring most organic revenue; list them and protect them before any change (no handle changes, no template experiments on them first).

Pages at positions 4 to 15 with top-tier impressions and a click rate below the store's own curve at that position: the title does not match what the searcher wants (price, range size, 'for X' wording).
Two store URLs taking turns on one query (collection vs product, two near-identical collections): split signals; pick one primary page per term.
Products linked from grids as /collections/x/products/y: every product exists at two URLs and internal links point at the duplicate.
'Crawled, currently not indexed' on product pages with supplier copy or near-empty collections: Google sees no reason to keep them.

Searched sub-categories with no page of their own (a material, use, size, price band or 'for whom' variant) whose queries land on a broad collection or a single product: the cheapest new pages to win.
The page type mismatch: a blog post chasing a grid query, or a collection chasing a guide query; the live results show which wins.
When rivals outrank, name the one gap that explains it: more products on the grid, an intro and guide, more internal links, better titles, or many more referring domains. Only the last needs links.
Blog posts with traffic and no clicks to products: wrong intent or no early product link; fix or fold into a guide.
Seasonal categories read year on year, never month on month.
Pages that hold position but lose clicks: check the results page for AI answers and shopping units before rewriting anything.

hypothesis_patterns.pattern: A near-win page with a weak snippet
hypothesis_patterns.evidence: position 4 to 10, impressions in the store's top tier, click rate below its own curve for that position
hypothesis_patterns.bet: Rewrite title, meta description and H1 to the searcher's wording, add 3 to 5 internal links from strong pages; read clicks after 4 weeks

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: queries with impressions and a cost per click land on a broad collection or one product; the results page shows grids
hypothesis_patterns.bet: One new indexable collection per searched variant with enough products, an intro, a short guide and links; read after 8 to 12 weeks

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: many products not indexed, duplicate paths in the crawl, tag or variant pages indexed
hypothesis_patterns.bet: Fix grid links and canonicals, 301 merged pages, noindex tag pages; confirm in the indexing report

hypothesis_patterns.pattern: Two pages fighting for one term
hypothesis_patterns.evidence: two URLs alternate for the same query in Search Console
hypothesis_patterns.bet: One primary page per term: merge with a 301 or give each a different intent

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: the store matches the top 3 on page type, products and copy, but sits far behind on referring domains
hypothesis_patterns.bet: Earned mentions (press, gift guides, stockists and suppliers) aimed at the collections ranking 4 to 10; a long build

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: posts with sessions, near-zero product clicks and purchases
hypothesis_patterns.bet: Rewrite the best ones into comparison or buying-guide shape with product links in the first screen; prune or merge the rest

decisions.ask: Quick wins, a long build, or both?

options.label: Quick wins only
options.pro: money in 2 to 6 weeks, little risk
options.con: capped by demand the store already touches
options.when: many pages sit at positions 4 to 15 and the team has little time

options.label: Quick wins first, then build one cluster (my usual pick)
options.pro: early proof pays for the build
options.con: two streams to manage
options.when: near-wins exist and the keyword map shows uncovered demand with a cost per click

options.label: Build one cluster now
options.con: 3 to 6 months before results
options.when: a young site with few impressions, or a new category

decisions.recommend: If indexing is broken, fix that first and nothing else counts yet. Then pick by the near-win list: enough impressions at positions 4 to 15 to matter in gross profit means the mix; almost none means the build.

decisions.ask: How do we close the gap to the pages that outrank you?

options.label: On-page only: titles, copy, structure, internal links
options.con: will not beat rivals with far more referring domains
options.when: the gap is page type, copy or links inside the site

options.label: On-page plus earned mentions (press, gift guides, stockists, suppliers)
options.con: slow, needs outreach and samples
options.when: on-page parity is reached and the referring-domain gap is large

options.label: Paid link placements
options.con: Google treats paid links that pass ranking credit as spam; a penalty can wipe out the gain
options.when: never as our recommendation; listed so the owner knows why

decisions.recommend: Compare the store's top collection with the top 3 results on page type, products shown, copy and referring domains. Recommend earned mentions only when everything except referring domains is at parity.

rules: One primary term per page, and no two store pages for the same intent.
Never change a handle without a 301 and updated internal links; never remove a page that earns clicks or links without a redirect.
Every new collection has enough products to be useful, its own intro and guide, and a reason to exist in search demand; no pages made in bulk for every tag.
Copy is for the buyer first: the term early in the title and H1, then plain facts; no keyword lists in copy or alt text.
Theme changes go on a duplicate theme, tested, then published.
Rank every fix by the gross profit of the pages it touches x the impressions at stake, and state when each should show (weeks for snippets and links, months for new pages).
Each change gets a baseline window and a read date with the same number of days, year on year for seasonal pages.

checks: Each changed template passes the Rich Results Test and a URL Inspection live test shows the main text without JavaScript.
Every changed or merged URL is in the redirect sheet, and no redirect chains are created.
senior_review: Is the baseline non-branded, and does the plan say what brand clicks did separately?
Did we read the live results page before choosing each page type?
Does every page we touch have one primary term, with no other store page competing for it?
Is every change ranked by gross profit, with its expected time to show and a read date?
Would any change drop a page that earns clicks or links without a redirect?
What did we assume that the owner's data contradicts (a margin, a bestseller, a market)?

Brand voice and product facts come from the org context and the catalogue.

files: Keyword map (CSV): one primary term per page, volume, cost per click, intent, current position, gross profit per month.
Collection SEO sheet ready to paste into Shopify, and the new collections to create with their rules.
Technical fix list with who does each fix and how to confirm it, plus a developer brief for theme changes.
Redirect sheet (CSV in Shopify's import format) for every changed or merged URL.
Internal link sheet: page, link to add, anchor text, placement.
Baseline and 90-day plan: non-branded clicks and organic gross profit today, each change with its read date.
next_moves: Comparison and buying-guide pages for the chosen cluster.
An AI answers baseline, to see whether assistants name the store for the same buying questions.
Product page copy for the top-profit products in the cluster.
A monthly Search Console read on the planned dates, with keep, change or stop per change.
